audit.whatIsWrong: Four fabricated names and one wrong cooldown claim across the content layer: 'Chaos Orb', 'Mystic Shot', 'Deathfire Grasp' (twice), 'Cutpurse-Sailor's Guardian', and 'punish the long cooldown' applied to Wild Cards.
audit.why: Chaos Orb is not a LeBlanc ability. Mystic Shot is Ezreal's. Deathfire Grasp has not been in the game for years. 'Cutpurse-Sailor's Guardian' is not an item. And Wild Cards is 6/5.75/5.5/5.25/5 — the shortest cooldown in his kit, not a long one, which inverts the whole piece of advice.
audit.corrected: Named the real tools: the sigil and its detonation, Pick a Card's gold card at 200 range with an auto-attack reset, Wild Cards on a 6-second cycle you bait rather than wait out, Loaded Dice gold, and Destiny's reveal.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Bait it with your W clone' and 'Bait Wild Cards with W-clone' attribute the clone to LeBlanc's W.
audit.why: W is Distortion, a dash with a 4-second return. The clone is Mirror Image, the passive, which triggers when she drops below 40% Health and lasts up to 8 seconds — it is not something you cast to bait with on demand.
audit.corrected: Bait Wild Cards on its 6-second cooldown; use Mirror Image when the passive actually fires, and send it where he expects you to run.

edits.before: - Twisted Fate Pick a Card (Gold): matchup-defining — The locked gold card starts every trade and gank — back off the moment it glows yellow. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget W Distortion (return) for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Pick a Card: 6s at every rank, so the gold card is never far away — back off when it locks yellow, then step up the moment it is spent. - Wild Cards: 6s at rank 1, 5s at rank 5. - Destiny: 170s at rank 1, so his global pick threat carries a real bill.

edits.before: You out-trade TF at levels 1-2 as long as you respect his Wild Card poke — bait it with your W clone, then punish the long cooldown with Sigil-empowered Q-E all-in. His card-flip randomness means he often can't guarantee Blue Card damage, so most exchanges before level 3 favor your burst combo if you play from max range.
edits.after: You out-trade TF at levels 1-2 as long as you respect his Wild Cards poke — it is only a 6-second cooldown, so bait it and step in the instant it is spent rather than waiting for a gap that never comes. His card-flip randomness means he often can't guarantee Blue Card mana back, so most exchanges before level 3 favor your burst if you play from max range.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 are your strongest window: Distortion lets you dash in, burst, and blink back out before Gold Card can land its stun, and Mystic Shot follow-up chip damage adds up over his passive gold sustain. At 6, his Destiny grants global vision and pick threat, but you still win any direct 1v1 if you catch him without a card ready — bait the flip, then all-in.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 are your strongest window: Distortion lets you dash in, burst, and blink back out before Gold Card can land its stun at 200 range, and the sigil detonation chips faster than his Loaded Dice gold buys back. At 6, Destiny grants global vision and pick threat on a 170-second cooldown, but you still win any 1v1 if you catch him without a card ready — bait the flip, then all-in.

edits.before: Once TF hits his first item and later Destiny is always up, his job shifts to setting up picks across the map rather than dueling you, so your late-game task is denying him easy Destiny angles by warding and grouping early. In teamfights you still delete him in one rotation if you can flank through stealth before his Deathfire Grasp or Gold Card connects on your frontline.
edits.after: Once TF hits his first item and Destiny drops to 110 seconds, his job shifts to setting up picks across the map rather than dueling you, so your late task is denying him easy Destiny angles by warding and grouping early. In teamfights you still delete him in one rotation if you flank before his gold card connects — but remember Destiny reveals every champion, so it strips your angle too.

notes: This matchup carried the worst fabrications in my slice — four invented or long-dead names in the content layer: 'Chaos Orb' (not a LeBlanc ability), 'Mystic Shot' (Ezreal's), 'Deathfire Grasp' twice (an item removed from the game years ago), and 'Cutpurse-Sailor's Guardian' (not an item). All four are now replaced with tools that exist. A fifth error was mechanical rather than nominal: 'punish the long cooldown' was applied to Wild Cards, which at 6/5.75/5.5/5.25/5 is the SHORTEST cooldown in his kit — the advice told a player to wait for a gap that never arrives, so it is now 'bait it and step in the instant it is spent'. Sixth: two fields attributed LeBlanc's clone to her W. W is Distortion; the clone is Mirror Image, the passive, which fires on its own below 40% Health and cannot be cast to bait with. Also newly on the page: Destiny reveals all enemy champions, which cuts against LeBlanc's flank angle and was never mentioned. PACKET SUSPECTNAME FALSE POSITIVE: the packet flagged 'Gold Card' in spikes[1].text as a probable wrong name matching 'wild cards'. It is correct — the gold card is a Pick a Card selection — and I left it. It also flagged 'Wild Card' in early, which WAS wrong (the ability is Wild Cards, plural) and is fixed. I also fixed the same singular in whys[0], which the packet did not flag. Level chart needed no edits: phases[N].side, win[N] and packet.levelChart all already read LeBlanc on all seven rows — the only matchup in my slice where the two layers agreed on arrival. I did not touch spikes[0].text's reference to LeBlanc's Q by name; I rewrote it to say 'the sigil' rather than substitute a name, because the brief's ownerKit gives slots and text but no ability names, and I would rather be nameless than wrong.
